recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-37714 unless a future work-group decision reopens whether particular standard SearchParameter definitions should use processingMode=other for non-default indexing behavior.
issue_request: FHIR-37714 was a Published FHIR-core Change Request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking that the Search page clarify how string search parameters such as Patient.name, Person.name, Practitioner.name, RelatedPerson.name, address, and similar complex-element parameters should be interpreted when the registry type is string but the expression points to a complex datatype.
initial_application: Commit ee10be816c added the requested source/search.html prose, Patient.name/HumanName example, and an xpathUsage/processingMode note. Commit 28782409d0 cleaned the R5 TODO to SearchParameter.processingMode, while later search-page commits 6941dfafeb and a3766ac36c preserved the rule in a general Matching and Sub-Elements section and conformance-tagged wording.
additional_context: Confluence minutes show FHIR-I deferred the item for proposed language on 2022-07-25 and approved it 13-0-0 on 2022-08-01. Current source/search.html contains both the general complex/backbone search guidance and the string-specific guidance requested by the Jira. The registry page links readers to Search guidance, and checked Patient/Person/Practitioner/RelatedPerson name parameters remain string search parameters over HumanName with descriptions of server-selected string fields. Zulip search found only FHIR-19692 sort-behavior background; broader Jira search found FHIR-48481, already represented on the combined branch and not changing this rule.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current built source already conveys the accepted clarification, including the default search against selected string-valued sub-elements, the option to point expressions directly at sub-elements, the Patient.name example, and the SearchParameter.processingMode guidance.

related_jiras.note: A later Zulip sort-behavior thread cited FHIR-37714 as guidance for complex/repeating search scenarios, but FHIR-19692 concerns sorting rather than the string search parameter registry clarification.
This later Applied issue clarifies derived SearchParameter rules, including preserving processingMode; it is already represented on the combined branch and does not change the FHIR-37714 rule.
